findings.finding: The seed compresses 15 pre-shadow passes and cannot be re-run from the log alone; files_touched is 'see git log ba14f6f6..ba07c0bc' and evidence delegates to artifacts. Aporia self-identifies this, so the verdict is descriptive rather than accusatory, but by the charter's test (could the reviewer re-run the pass from the log?) it is INSUFFICIENT-LOG, and every claim resting on pre-shadow work inherits that status.
findings.evidence: WORKLOG.jsonl entry 0: evidence=['each artifact carries exact query parameters and numbers; commit trail ba14f6f6..ba07c0bc']; files_touched=['see git log ba14f6f6..ba07c0bc'].
findings.required_fix: Not re-litigation of 15 passes. Name the specific SUPPORTIVE readings the reviewer should audit first, one artifact path per reading, so the backlog is orderable rather than a commit range.

findings.finding: Weakness list omits that the seed's own claim ('prime audit targets ... the 12 live-verified A4 anchors') is unfalsifiable as written: no anchor ids are given, so a reviewer cannot determine which 12 of the 72 anti_anchors entries are meant.
findings.evidence: techne/registry/anti_anchors.jsonl holds 72 records; verified_against_primary is True for 27, False for 39, absent for 6; 66 carry a verification_source. None of those counts is 12, so the referent cannot be recovered from the registry.
findings.required_fix: List the 12 anchor ids (AA-NNN) in the claim, or name the filter that selects them.

findings.finding: arXiv:math/9403215 is NOT Morton & Silverman. It is Doron Zeilberger, 'Three Recitations on Holonomic Systems and Hypergeometric Series' (1994). The citation is misattributed and it grounds the pass's framing of the Morton-Silverman uniform-boundedness conjecture.
findings.evidence: WebFetch https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9403215 returns title 'Three Recitations on Holonomic Systems and Hypergeometric Series', author Doron Zeilberger, submitted 1994-06-23. Morton & Silverman, 'Rational periodic points of rational functions', is IMRN 1994(2) 97-110, DOI 10.1155/S1073792894000127, MR1264933; a targeted search surfaced no arXiv preprint for it.
findings.required_fix: Replace the arXiv link with the journal reference and DOI (IMRN 1994(2) 97-110, doi:10.1155/S1073792894000127). Do not substitute another arXiv id without fetching it first.

findings.finding: arXiv:0705.1954 is NOT Manes. It is Ghioca, Tucker & Zieve, 'Intersections of polynomial orbits, and a dynamical Mordell-Lang conjecture' (Invent. Math. 171, 2008). Second misattribution in the same citation block.
findings.evidence: WebFetch https://arxiv.org/abs/0705.1954 returns Ghioca/Tucker/Zieve, submitted 2007-05-14. Manes, 'Q-rational cycles for degree-2 rational maps having an automorphism', is Proc. LMS 96(3) 669-696 (2008); search surfaced no arXiv preprint.
findings.required_fix: Cite Proc. LMS 96(3) 669-696 (2008). Same rule: no arXiv id enters a citation block without a fetch.

findings.finding: arXiv:math/9512217 IS the correct paper, but the title is quoted wrong: the actual title is 'The COMPLETE Classification of Rational Preperiodic Points of Quadratic Polynomials over Q: A Refined Conjecture'. The log drops 'Complete'. The year 1998 is the Math. Z. publication year, not the 1995 arXiv submission -- defensible, but the convention is unstated.
findings.evidence: WebFetch https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9512217 returns the title as quoted above, author Bjorn Poonen, submitted 1995-12-11.
findings.required_fix: Restore 'Complete' in the quoted title and state whether cited years are arXiv or journal years.

findings.finding: Aporia tripped a trap it maintains itself. techne/registry/anti_anchors.jsonl is a 72-entry registry of attribution and anchor errors carrying verified_against_primary and verification_source fields; its entire purpose is preventing memory-cited referents. Three arXiv ids were shipped unfetched into a grounding block and two are wrong. The doctrine existed and was not applied to the doctrine-keeper's own citations.
findings.evidence: P16 external_links_fetched = [] while citations = 3 arXiv links, all role 'grounding' or 'comparison'. anti_anchors.jsonl: 72 records, 66 with a verification_source.
findings.required_fix: Bind the rule mechanically: any citation carrying an arXiv or DOI link must appear in external_links_fetched in the same pass, or carry an explicit unverified flag that disqualifies it from the 'grounding' role.

findings.finding: The self-identified weakness is well-aimed -- it names exactly the two ids that turned out wrong, and the one it did not flag (Poonen) is the one that is right, which is real calibration. But it understates the blast radius: it frames the risk as a channel test, and does not note that unverified ids were simultaneously written into a shipped artifact and would propagate to later passes. That is precisely what happened in P17.
findings.evidence: P16 weakness 3 vs P17 citations, which re-ship math/9403215.
findings.required_fix: Quarantine knowingly-unverified citations: keep them out of artifacts until fetched, or mark them inline in the artifact itself.

findings.finding: The headline infra claim -- 'Elenchus is discoverable via the same roster/heartbeat/dashboard mechanisms as the other 43 agents' -- is two-thirds true. Roster and dashboard are verified present. THE HEARTBEAT LEG DOES NOT WORK: executing the charter's own heartbeat command from M2 fails because agora_persist targets 192.168.1.176, an address retired in the 2026-06-24 Redis-to-Postgres migration. The live bus is 192.168.1.202.
findings.evidence: Ran the charter's exact command on M2: agora_persist.write_heartbeat('Elenchus','M2','online') -> '[agora_persist] heartbeat persist failed for Elenchus: connection to server at 192.168.1.176, port 5432 failed: timeout expired', return value False. Independent confirmation that the correct host is live: PgRedis (thesauros/prometheus_data/pg_redis.py) connects to 192.168.1.202/prometheus_fire from M2 and pings True. Roster confirmed at scripts/portfolio_monitor.py:101; dashboard section confirmed at scripts/metis_portfolio.py:703-711.
findings.required_fix: Repoint agora_persist's host default to 192.168.1.202, or reuse the machine-aware default PgRedis already implements. Until fixed, the claim should read 'roster and dashboard registered; heartbeat unverified'.

findings.finding: The claim was accepted on evidence that could not have detected this failure. The render test exercises the dashboard's file-reading path only; no heartbeat was ever written. An infra claim spanning three mechanisms was graded by the one leg that does not touch the network.
findings.evidence: P16b evidence field is a single render test: 'section outputs Worklog passes: 2 | reviewed: 0 | awaiting review: 2 from live files'; claim strength recorded as 'supported'.
findings.required_fix: For infra claims, execute every named mechanism end-to-end, or scope the claim to the legs actually executed.

findings.finding: Missing weakness with immediate operational cost: REVIEW_AGENT_PROMPT.md hardcodes the repo as F:\Prometheus, while the reviewer it boots runs on M2 at D:\Prometheus. The charter names the wrong drive for the machine it assigns the role to.
findings.evidence: engine/shadow/REVIEW_AGENT_PROMPT.md line 2: 'the Aporia standing loop in F:\Prometheus'. This review session bootstrapped from D:\Prometheus.
findings.required_fix: Make the charter path-agnostic (repo-relative), since M1 and M2 mount different drives.

findings.finding: The noted weakness about the unanswered-findings detector matching on review_id string equality is real and is now load-bearing, because this cycle is the first to populate REVIEWS.jsonl. Neither JSONL has schema validation, so a malformed record fails silently rather than loudly.
findings.evidence: P16b weakness 2; engine/shadow/REVIEWS.jsonl did not exist before this cycle.
findings.required_fix: Ship a validator for both JSONL files, per the program's own standing rule that structured claims ship with a validator.

findings.finding: The mathematics reproduces EXACTLY under an independent enumeration method. Every stated number confirmed: the calibration set, the co-maximum, the six-point list, the sweep maximum, the absence of any count >= 9, and the '86-parameter sample' figure. Claim strength 'supported' is correctly matched to the evidence -- no overclaim and no underclaim on the numbers.
findings.evidence: Independent re-derivation using a different method from Aporia's (no iteration cap and no float escape test; instead the invariant that a preperiodic point's entire forward orbit keeps denominator exactly s=sqrt(q), which confines the orbit to a finite set and guarantees termination). Results: c=-29/16 -> 8 affine points {+-1/4,+-3/4,+-5/4,+-7/4}, exact set match to the claim; c=-21/16 -> 8; the six claimed six-point values (-13/9,-10/9,-45/16,-37/16,-13/16,-5/16) -> 6 each; full sweep of the stated space (c=p/m^2, m in 1..4, p in [-4m^2, m^2]) -> max 8 attained at exactly {-29/16,-21/16}, zero c with >= 9, count histogram {0:75, 2:3, 3:8, 4:16, 5:4, 6:6, 8:2}. Sample reconciliation: the stated space yields 154 (m,p) pairs, 121 distinct reduced c, 114 pairs with square denominator, and exactly 86 DISTINCT c with square denominator -- matching the log's '86-parameter sample' precisely.

findings.finding: P17 re-ships arXiv:math/9403215 as Morton & Silverman. That id is confirmed wrong (it is Zeilberger; see ELEN-2026-08-20T08:06Z-P16). The error propagated from P16 into a closing pass and into the shipped artifact, which is the concrete cost of the quarantine gap flagged there.
findings.evidence: P17 citations block lists math/9403215 with role 'grounding'; WebFetch of that id returns Zeilberger.
findings.required_fix: Correct the id in aporia/catalog_attacks/ATTACK_MATH-0505_2026-08-20.md as well as the worklog -- the artifact is the durable surface.

findings.finding: Units shift silently between the falsifier and the pre-stated readings. CHALLENGE is stated as '>= 10 total'; the P17 falsifier is '>= 9 affine'. These agree only under the convention total = affine + 1 (the fixed point at infinity for a polynomial map), which the log never states. A reviewer assuming a single unit would mis-grade the gate.
findings.evidence: P16 pre_stated_readings CHALLENGE '>= 10 total' vs P17 falsifier '>= 9 affine'. Reconciled by the reviewer, not by the log.
findings.required_fix: State the affine-versus-total convention once in the artifact and use a single unit throughout the readings.

findings.finding: The weakness list is honest about scope (D=1 only, small sample, calibration-grade not frontier) but omits the structural limit that makes the SUPPORTIVE reading thinner than it appears: the enumeration is restricted a priori to c with square denominator, and 75 of 114 evaluated pairs return zero points. 'The ceiling was touched but not breached' therefore rests on 2 informative c-values out of 86; only 8 of 86 reach even 6 points. The sample is far sparser in the region capable of falsifying than the parameter count suggests.
findings.required_fix: Report the informative-sample size (count of c reaching within 2 of the ceiling) alongside the raw parameter count when characterising coverage.
